newsitem.title: UNITED NATIONS: U.N. council protests Tajikistan hostage-taking.
newsitem.headline: U.N. council protests Tajikistan hostage-taking.

text.p: Security Council members strongly condemned the seizure on Friday by Tajik guerrillas of 23 hostages, including seven U.N. military observers, and appealed for their immediate release.
The incident followed one last Sunday in which four U.N. observers were abused and subjected to a mock execution by Tajik government troops at a checkpoint.

"The members of the council have instructed me to express their firm and resolute condemnation of this repeated cowardly act and to appeal for an immediate and unconditional release of all the hostages," council President Francesco Paolo Fulci of Italy told reporters after a briefing on the incident by a senior U.N. official.
Tens of thousands of people have been killed in a four-year civil war between Tajikistan's secular government and Islamist guerrillas.

A 96-member U.N. Mission of Observers in Tajikistan (UNMOT), whose mandate was renewed for four months by the Security Council last week, works with a much larger peacekeeping force fielded by the Commonwealth of Independent States.
In the latest incident, an armed group held up a column of U.N. personnel, Tajik government officials and representatives of the Islamic opposition.
The armed group demanded that the rebels free the brother of an opposition leader, Rizvon Sadirov, who joined forces with the government last month.

The group said the hostages would be shot if their demands were not met by 2 pm local time (0900 GMT) on Sunday. They also threatened to detonate 30 bombs planted at various points around Dushanbe, the Tajik capital, if any attempt were made to interfere.

Fulci said he was calling in Tajikistan's U.N. envoy, ambassador Rashid Alimov, for the second time in two days. On Thursday he informed the envoy of the "great concern of the United Nations over the extremely troubling developments of the last few days," he added.
